channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Iran Extends Blackout of Nuclear Work With US War Deadlocked
item.description: Iran extended its shutout of United Nations nuclear inspectors, deepening the lack of international knowledge of the country’s uranium stockpile with no sign of fresh talks with the US.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Tirone

item.title: Cameron: Do ‘Whatever It Takes’ to Tackle Migration
item.description: Former British Prime Minister David Cameron says centrist politicians in the UK have not done enough to tackle small boats and illegal migration. Speaking on The Mishal Husain show, he advocates for the UK to leave the European Convention on Human Rights. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia Replaces Huang as Lutnick Faces Scrutiny on China
item.description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from Berlin, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.
Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang, the preeminent face of the AI infrastructure boom, was ousted from his post after reports of three affairs, including one with a woman suspected of spying for China. Longtime Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress is taking the job of interim CEO, Nvidia said on Thursday
Anthropic initial public offering has drawn about six times the orders for the shares available, according to people familiar with the matter, as interest increases for potentially the biggest first-time share sale ever.
Today's guest: Madeleine Ronner, DWS, Senior Portfolio Manager, Global Equities. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia Crisis to Bring More US Chip Regulation, Says DWS's Ronner
item.description: Madeleine Ronner, Senior Portfolio Manager, Global Equities at DWS, says she expects more scrutiny to come regarding US chip export controls to countries like China. It follows the ousting of Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO after he was accused of multiple affairs, including one woman suspected of spying for China. Ronner was speaking to Bloomberg TV's Daybreak Europe. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Zelenskyy Says Talks With US Envoys in Dublin Made Progress
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said progress had been made during a meeting with US envoys in Ireland, hailing a prisoner swap deal and a decision to include Europeans in the next round of peace talks with Russia. Bloomberg's Greg Sullivan reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: David Cameron: I Love Public Service
item.description: The former UK prime minister discusses the race to cure Alzheimer’s, Brexit 10 years on and whether he’d return to government again. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: David Cameron Calls for UK to Leave European Human Rights Convention
item.description: Former Prime Minister David Cameron said the UK should leave the European Convention on Human Rights, associating himself with a hardline anti-immigration position that would once have been anathema to the UK’s mainstream political right.
item.dc:creator: Chloe Chaplain

item.title: Thailand Seeks Access to Myanmar Mines Linked to River Pollution
item.description: Thailand plans to send a minister to Myanmar to investigate suspected mining sites blamed for contaminating rivers that flow across the border as it steps up efforts to trace pollution that has threatened drinking water and farmland.
item.dc:creator: Erich Parpart

item.title: Philippines’ VP Duterte Drops 16 Witnesses for Her Impeachment Trial
item.description: Lawyers for Philippine Vice President Sara Duterte, facing impeachment charges that she failed to truthfully disclose her assets, dropped plans to tap financial executives as witnesses about millions of pesos in bank transactions.
item.dc:creator: Ditas B Lopez

item.title: Foreign Businesses Putin Seized Help Fund Russia’s War Machine
item.description: Russian units of foreign companies seized by the Kremlin are helping to pay for President Vladimir Putin’s war in Ukraine.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: How Huang’s Exit Could Lead to Nvidia Slowdown
item.description: Bloomberg Economics' geonomics and technology analyst Michael Deng says former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was capable of operating across the China-US divide and his departure may expose Nvidia to government policy from both sides. Huang, who made frequent visits to China and lobbied the US government for looser restrictions on chip exports to China, was ousted from his post after reports of three affairs. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Van Hollen Challenges Schumer for Senate Leader in New Congress
item.description: Senator Chris Van Hollen, a progressive from Maryland, is challenging Chuck Schumer to become Senate majority leader in the new Congress, after rising demands in the party for a bolder, more populist agenda in the wake of historic Democratic victories.
item.dc:creator: Steven T. Dennis

item.title: Nvidia Crisis Prompts Scrutiny of Lutnick’s Role in Chip Policy
item.description: Fallout from Jensen Huang’s ouster as Nvidia Corp. chief executive officer is reaching deep into Washington, where Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has drawn scrutiny over whether his department did enough to keep the company’s prized artificial intelligence chips out of China’s hands.
item.dc:creator: Alicia Diaz and Maggie Eastland

item.title: Nvidia Fallout Looms Over Trump-Xi Meeting
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Rep. Gregory Meeks (D-NY) says he wants to know when former CEO Jensen Huang was informed by the US government that the woman he was having an affair with was allegedly involved in Chinese espionage and why Nvidia was not notified sooner. Michael Allen, Managing Director of Beacon Global Strategies and former special assistant to President George W. Bush in the National Security sector, thinks Congress needs to direct its questions to the Commerce Department and, by extension, the National Security Council process staff about what happened with export-control regulations and what may have held them up. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Allen Says US Needs Stronger Export-Control Enforcement
item.description: Michael Allen, Managing Director of Beacon Global Strategies and former special assistant to President George W. Bush in the National Security sector, thinks Congress needs to direct its questions to the Commerce Department and, by extension, the National Security Council process staff about what happened with export-control regulations and what may have held them up. Allen says stronger export controls and beefing up the Department of Commerce are important, including greater enforcement, oversight and investigations. Allen says Trump should make clear to President Xi Jinping that China’s activity involving smuggling and restricted technology could lead Congress to take further action. He speaks with Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: The Debrief: Lutnick Faces Scrutiny Over Chip Export Controls
item.description: Bloomberg’s Mario Parker joined the show for, The Debrief, to discuss Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick facing scrutiny over what he knew about Nvidia and China, tensions inside the White House and questions about his standing in the administration. He speaks with Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rep. Meeks Says Questions Remain Over Nvidia Warning
item.description: Rep. Gregory Meeks (D-NY) says he wants to know when former CEO Jensen Huang was informed by the US government that the woman he was having an affair with was allegedly involved in Chinese espionage and why Nvidia was not notified sooner. Rep. Meeks says the issue is not just the affair, but what information might have been given to China and others that could endanger US national security. Rep. Meeks says Congress needs to determine what the administration knew and why Nvidia may not have been notified, as well as examine questions involving Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. He speaks with Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Jokowi Era Fades in Indonesia With Son Forced Out as Prabowo’s Vice President
item.description: The ultimate target of President Prabowo Subianto’s shakeup at the top of Indonesian politics may be the man who helped propel him to power after leading the country for a decade: ex-President Joko Widodo.
item.dc:creator: Ben Otto, Rosalind Mathieson and Claire Jiao

item.title: SEC Investigates T1 Energy’s Disclosures of Tax Credits
item.description: T1 Energy Inc. said it’s being probed by the US Securities and Exchange Commission over the solar company’s disclosures related to its eligibility for clean energy manufacturing tax credits and other accounting matters.
item.dc:creator: Mark Chediak

item.title: Trump Bets Shaky Iran Status Quo Will Hold After Midterm Loss
item.description: President Donald Trump has floated a new strategy for his war against Iran: leave the conflict in limbo and walk away.
item.dc:creator: Eric Martin, Courtney McBride and Fiona MacDonald
